title: eludite.debug.pause input
description: Debug > Break All (Ctrl+Alt+Break): stop a running debuggee wherever it is, for example when it hangs or loops. Only while it runs; refused in any other mode. Nothing changes until the adapter reports the stop (reason `pause`); then it is shown as any break. From an agent it waits like a resuming command and answers the stop summary (debug-stop-summary.output.json); the pause point is often in external code, so read `frames` and use eludite.debug.stack or eludite.debug.snapshot with `frame` to find your code.

thread.description: The thread to pause. Default: the last thread that stopped, else 0 (all threads; adapters pause every thread anyway).

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for the debuggee to break before answering, in milliseconds. From the UI the command never waits; from another thread (an agent) the default is 5000.

depth.description: How many levels of the locals to expand: 1 (default) lists the top level only; up to 5. Expansion is breadth-first and stops when `max_variables` rows are listed.

max_variables.description: The most variable rows listed, counting every level (default 50, at most 500).

max_value_chars.description: Values longer than this are cut and end with `… (N chars)`, the row saying `value_truncated` (default 200, at most 10000).

max_frames.description: The most stack frames listed (default 10, at most 200); page further with eludite.debug.stack.

max_output_lines.description: The most program output lines listed (default 20, at most 1000; 0 lists none).

output_since.description: An output cursor (`output.next` of an earlier answer, or eludite.debug.output's `next`): list the program's lines from it on. Default: the last `max_output_lines` lines.
